$comment: Single source of truth for the CPAL-1.0 Section 14 Attribution Information.
Keep the React component, ATTRIBUTION.md, Exhibit A and Exhibit B in LICENSE in sync.
scripts/license.test.mjs checks their key attribution values.
Changing any value here is a license change - update LICENSE in the same commit.
graphicImage is the ONE image Exhibit B declares, which is the legal floor.
variants are alternatives we additionally permit, so that nobody has a
legitimate reason to edit the mark to fit their theme.
The mark is the full horizontal lockup - icon plus wordmark - because that
is the complete LinkSense identity. The phrase is therefore just 'Powered
by': the name is carried by the wordmark inside the logo, so pairing it with
'Powered by LinkSense' would print the name twice.
BECAUSE THE NAME LIVES IN THE IMAGE, imageAltText is not decorative - it is
what keeps the notice readable when the image fails to load, and what screen
readers announce. It must never be empty.
Do not point graphicImage at the app icon or favicon: those are separate
assets with a different job (see docs/brand/), and redesigning one must not
silently change what the license requires.
No typeface is specified on purpose. The notice inherits the host
application's font: a credit that imports a webfont to look correct is an
external dependency that fails in exactly the air-gapped deployments we
target, and a licensed typeface would make compliance impossible for
downstream users. What is specified instead is a legibility floor.
placement mirrors Exhibit B, 'When and Where Displayed'. CPAL 14(a) names a
dedicated attribution area on user interface screens as a recognised form,
and adds that continued use of the form the Original Code uses is one way of
meeting the requirement - so the form we ship is the form downstream copies.
Full-screen modes, transient overlays and generated exports are exempt on
purpose: a rule that fights the host application's own layout gets removed.
